articles.title: Dungeons & Dragons Takes Inspiration from Live-Service Video Games, With a New Plan For Themed Seasonal Releases
articles.summary: Dungeons & Dragons is taking a page out of the live-service video game play book by introducing themed seasonal content updates. New expansions, sourcebooks and other products will be tied into unifying themes, beginning in April with a three-month "Season of Horror."
articles.body:
Dungeons & Dragons is taking a page out of the live-service video game play book by introducing themed seasonal content updates. New expansions, sourcebooks and other products will be tied into unifying themes, beginning in April with a three-month "Season of Horror."

The tabletop titan has decided to group all of its major product releases through the rest of 2026 into distinct seasons, each anchored by a major book release (thanks, Nerdvana ). Even this year's product roadmap looks like something released by Bungie or Blizzard:

Running from April until June, Dungeons & Dragon's inaugural Season of Horror will include the long-awaited return to Ravenloft in a fresh sourcebook, Ravenloft: The Horrors Within, which promises creepy new subclasses, species, backgrounds and Dark Gift feats. Priced $59.99, it launches in June, and will be accompanied by the tarot-inspired Tarokka card deck ($24.99), and a Horrors Within DM screen ($24.99) and map pack ($24.99).

Next up, from July through September, is the Season of Magic. This will include the Arcana Unleashed sourcebook (available in September, priced $49.99) that details high-magic character creator options and a new system for magic items that lets them grow in power alongside your character level. The season will also add Arcana Unleashed: Deadfall, a Red Wizard-themed adventure expansion ($29.99), and further cards.

Finally for 2026, the Season of Champions will pick up from October through December — though its range of themed products is yet to be revealed.

Earlier this year, former Nintendo of America boss Doug Bowser joined the board of Hasbro , the company which owns D&D publisher Wizards of the Coast. D&D continues to enjoy huge interest, helped in turn by the breakout success of Baldur's Gate 3 . Previous comments from Hasbro have suggested that another Baldur's Gate game will follow at some point , once a studio to make it has been found. Meanwhile, a Baldur's Gate TV series is in the works for HBO .

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.summary: Preorders have gone live for the new Dungeons & Dragons Ravenloft: The Horrors Within expansion, including the expansion book, DM screen, map pack, and Tarokka deck.
articles.body:
For those ready to gather their D&D party and venture forth for a spooky adventure, the new Dungeons & Dragons Ravenloft: The Horrors Within expansion will set you on the right path. Complete with a gameplay expansion book ($59.99), DM screen ($24.99), map pack ($24.99), and Tarokka deck ($24.99), the full expansion is now available to preorder with a release date of June 16.

As someone who loves both horror and D&D, I think this looks like a delightfully creepy new adventure to embark on. The expansion book highlights 16 Domains of Dread, 17 Darklords with their own stat blocks, new subclasses, and Dark Gift feats that players have to look forward to.

The map pack comes with 10 horror-themed battle maps to create a thrilling journey as well, and the Tarokka deck can show you what the future holds - whether that be run-ins with a Darklord or brand new Domains of Dread. Of course, all of these feature astonishing artwork as well. I mean, for instance, how could you not love that portrait of Strahd on the cover of the expansion book? I think it's excellent.

This new expansion is part of Dungeons & Dragon's Season of Horror, which kicked off this month and runs until June as part of D&D's new themed seasonal content updates . Some familiar voices will be taking on this expansion soon as well.

Baldur's Gate 3's Neil Newbon and Devora Wilde - alongside DesiQuest's Jasmine Bhullar, Dispatch's Mayanna Berrin and 13 Reasons Why's Christian Navarro - will be playing through Ravenloft: The Horrors Within as part of the new D&D "actual play" show, Dungeon Masters . If you're curious to see what the new expansion is like, this seems like a great way to experience it through some very familiar voices.

Dungeons & Dragons maker Wizards of the Coast has fully unveiled its big crossover with World of Warcraft.

Announced this evening at Gen Con 2026, the D&D: Worldcraft expansion book will be accompanied by the Icecrown Citadel Map Pack, which takes characters from level 16 up to level 20.

World of Warcraft is the first D&D expansion under the new Universes Beyond banner, which brings third-party franchises together with classic tabletop gameplay. Created alongside Blizzard, D&D: WOW will bring Warcraft back to the tabletop for the first time in two decades.

Crafted using elements from across WOW lore, the expansion is designed for players keen to explore Azeroth during any of its eras, with a broad range of character choices, dungeons and quests available.

Impressively, the expansion book will include details of every playable WOW species and class (even Pandaren), as well as 26 magic items, seven iconic WOW dungeons, 30 dungeon boss stat blocks, 60+ new spells, 50+ new monsters, 23 factions with renown rewards, professions, mounts, companion creatures and more.

articles.body:
A new gameplay expansion book and other accessories are bringing World of Warcraft into Dungeons & Dragons. If you’re a fan of one or the other and want to check out the crossover, you can preorder the items now ahead of their November 17 release.

D&D: World of Warcraft - Gameplay Expansion Book

The main item you’ll need to cross the MMO and TTRPG streams is the D&D: WoW Gameplay Expansion Book. It transplants a ton of WoW-specific content into the tabletop RPG. It has rules for 16 new WoW-based species, all 13 classes from the MMO, plus nine new or revised subclasses and over 40 specializations. It also brings seven dungeons, over 50 new monsters, and 30 dungeon boss stat blocks, along with mounts, companion creatures, spells, magic items, and professions. Brothers and sisters, it’s a lot.

D&D: World of Warcraft - Icecrown Citadel Adventure Map Pack

The Lich King is probably the most iconic villain in the Warcraft universe, and he’s alive and well in this D&D campaign (but not for long, if you can help it). This adventure map pack includes everything you need to invade the Lich King’s Icecrown Citadel. It’s comprised of five chapters, 10 maps, and 10 boss encounters.

This four-panel DM screen helpfully hides the DM’s notes and papers. The outside of the screen is adorned with a gorgeous ultra-widescreen World of Warcraft painting. The screen’s inside is packed with handy information and reference tables you’ll want to have on hand when you’re running a game.

D&D campaigns can be run entirely with words, putting the game in the minds of the players. Or you can pick up some miniatures (which go along nicely with the maps above) to put the game on the table. Two packs are available, one with six Horde figures plus Illidan Stormrage and the other with six Alliance figures, plus the Lich King.

articles.title: Werner Herzog's Bucking Fastard Teams Real-Life Sisters Kate and Rooney Mara in an Unusual Almost True Story
articles.summary: Bucking Fastard review: Werner Herzog casts Kate and Rooney Mara as synchronized sisters based on unusual real-life twins.
articles.body:
This review is based on a screening at the Venice Film Festival. Bucking Fastard does not have a release date yet.

Basing his film loosely on Yorkshire twins Freda and Greta Chaplin, who notoriously spoke and moved in sync, Werner Herzog unfurls a real-life tale of codependence into a unique episodic drama about sheltered adults entering society for the very first time. The result, Bucking Fastard, is strange and wistful, verging occasionally on the surreal — it’s fittingly dedicated to David Lynch in its opening titles — and though its final notes lack the intended impact, the result is fantastical and worthwhile.

A large part of this comes down to the challenge of casting and directing such an idiosyncratic endeavor. Sisters Kate and Rooney Mara have had parallel careers which finally collide in Herzog’s latest. They play Jean and Joan Holbrooke — respectively, though it rarely matters. When the movie begins, the American siblings (“We’re not twins, we’re sisters,” they clarify emphatically and in unison) are placed on trial in Ireland, where they were raised, for stalking and harassing their suave neighbor, Mr. Mulroney (Orlando Bloom), who they claim to be in love with and married to after a number of eager threesomes. The stakes here are low — a restraining order rather than a criminal conviction — allowing the story to take on mischievous hues as their obsessions play out in flashbacks.

Two things become immediately clear during this opening act: one, that the Mara sisters are a delight to watch together, delivering overlapping or echoing dialogue interspersed with wry smiles and knowing looks at one another; two, that the Holbrookes have a tragically incomplete understanding of the world despite their attempts at sexual independence. They have an antiquated way of speaking, moving, and dressing, so much so that the movie’s time period is practically obscured. Freda and Greta’s own harassment trial was in the 1980s — the film’s title comes from a verbal slip they made together in court — so it’s easy to assume a similar setting on screen until the first iPhone appears some thirty minutes in (courtesy of a curious onlooker demanding a selfie once the sisters become local celebrities).

The real twins were the subjects of their own documentaries , but Herzog, who actually met them, circumvents the need or desire to craft a traditional biography. Instead, he extrapolates the isolation and self-loathing that he imagines might have defined their adult lives, as a pair of women so in tune with one another that they could barely communicate with the outside world or function apart. He also imbues his fictitious stand-ins with a certain naïveté of which men throughout the movie threaten to take advantage, creating an imposing uncertainty whenever the sisters step outside. In male-dominated pop culture, twin girls and women tend to occupy either a scary or salacious place; think the twin ghosts from The Shining, or the pornographic fantasy of bedding two identical women. These ideas loom large over the Holbrookes, as Herzog has them unknowingly wrestle with these forces during mundane interactions with men who are either devious or paternalistic, and whose benevolence might just come with invisible strings. Doubt always looms, even if the sisters seldom feel it themselves.

However, once the film moves on from their trial and follows their attempts at living alone — which is to say, just the two of them — it takes on a more subdued tone, and not without good reason. Bucking Fastard seldom delves into the details of their past, but instead reverse-engineers its drama from fleeting mentions of their complicated upbringing by parents we never see and who want little to do with them once their impish antics begin to encompass arson. The absence of real love and acceptance hovers over the Holbrookes, causing them to misunderstand their own feelings at every turn, even if what they feel is pure. They are, in a sense, alien — twin souls who have no one but each other since the world rejects them both.

The movie is at its most poignant once they move far away from society to the lush Irish countryside. Once the sisters visit their ailing aunt Louise (Marion O'Dwyer) and befriend her sweet, burdened neighbor, the elderly shepherd McFarlane (Brendan Conroy), Bucking Fastard presses pause on its whimsy so that Jean and Joan can more carefully reflect on what they want from humanity and what it gives them in return. The answer isn’t always kind, but this setting affords them poetic promises of escape via a local legend surrounding a nearby cave, which — although they don’t have the capacity to digest its fiction — sparks something deep within them.

The film has a bittersweet lust for life, which Herzog finds nestled in still and painterly scenes between his crowded fish-eye close ups and uncanny framing (the camera, fittingly, moves in sync with both his leads). And although its eventual abstractions don’t quite reach meaningful catharsis or enlightenment — if anything, it ends on a surprising downswing — Herzog’s gentle tragedy of two women cast out by the world veers between amusing and straightforwardly touching, like an adult fairy tale about yearning for connection.

articles.title: STALZONE Is an Extraction Shooter with MMO DNA
articles.body:
Back in June, developer EXBO rebranded free-to-play open-world PvPvE extraction shooter STALCRAFT: X as STALZONE alongside a graphical upgrade, reworking of its starting missions and locations, PvP rebalancing, and other big changes. The overhaul was designed to allow new players smooth entry to a game that’s been going strong for years and is a unique combination of different genres.

While STALZONE is an extraction shooter, it doesn’t play like most other games in the genre. You don’t simply drop into one self-contained map for a session. It’s a persistent world where factions fight over territory and the balance of power can shift while you’re offline. And there are NPCs, quests, and dungeons like you’d find in an MMORPG.

It takes place in the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone, which has been twisted by anomalies and overrun by mutants. You’ll use a detector to safely navigate the anomalies, and there are hidden caches and artifacts to find, constantly shifting weather, and global cataclysms like an energy emission that turns the sky red and can kill all living things.

The 50-hour story is told across two main campaigns, and the latest update added English voice acting. This is not an extraction shooter where you need to sift through item descriptions to decipher the world’s lore, it’s all laid out through the main story and the many side quests.

While STALZONE may have the quest design of an MMORPG, it doesn’t have the progression systems of one. You’re not going to gain experience points and gradually level up. Progression is built around acquiring and customizing new gear. There are more than 200 guns, which can be altered with a huge variety of attachments.

The primary way to acquire new gear is through trips into the Zone, but if you die before extracting your loot, you only lose what you gathered during that one trip. You don’t have to grind back from zero or risk losing your customized gear. So there’s still value to extracting and you can always keep progressing, but without the punishment for failure being too harsh.

You can also get new gear from other players either by trading with them directly or by using the auction house. You can buy and sell pretty much anything, and the player economy is expansive enough that you can get rich from buying and selling items at the right time to the right people.

When you take a trip into the Zone, global matchmaking will put you up against similarly geared opponents. Since there’s no leveling, there’s not a strict level matching system, but matchmaking will keep the gap between you and your opponents relatively small and EXBO’s in-house EXENS Anti-Cheat system keeps competition fair. That makes skill and positioning the most important factors in determining who walks away victorious.

STALZONE has remained consistently supported since its inception. EXBO is staffed with more than 400 employees, and they add updates every two weeks as well as regular seasonal events both big and small.

The rebrand in June marked the game’s biggest such update. In addition to the changes we already mentioned, it added new face models for characters that improved their emoting and lip syncing, introduced a light-source lighting system with better indoor lighting and more realistic-looking campfires and lamps, and added a new summer storyline.

STALZONE took part in The FPS Games Show today and unveiled its fall season content, which has transformed the Zone with autumn colors and began with a global cataclysm in the form of an electrical storm. The season also introduced the updated central location of the northern territories, Forge-11, and will soon continue with a major event dedicated to the cultist faction Covenant.

There's a special invite code available now for readers of this article to help you get started. Just activate code IGNWELCOME in-game to get several goodies, including weapons, consumables, days of premium access, and season pass levels (detailed in the image below).

STALZONE is available to play for free right now on PC, through Steam , Epic Games Store, and directly through the game’s official website , where you can also learn more about the game. For the latest news and updates, you can follow it on Discord , Twitter , and YouTube .

articles.title: Until Dawn 2 Was Co-Developed by Dispatch Developer AdHoc Studio
articles.summary: AdHoc Studio, the team behind Disptached, helped develop Until Dawn 2.
articles.body:
AdHoc Studio, the team behind Disptach, helped develop Until Dawn 2.

In a new PlayStation Blog post , Until Dawn 2 developer Firesprite confirmed that AdHoc helped craft the story of the new horror game. As a result, the team promises a much richer experience with tough choices that impact the branching narrative.

"We’ve partnered with our friends at AdHoc Studio – the brilliant minds behind the acclaimed Dispatch – so you can expect a deeply layered story packed with rich characters, razor-sharp dialogue, fraught relationships, tough decisions, and yes… more than a few gruesome deaths," reads the post. "Every choice, every interaction can ripple with dramatic consequences."

AdHoc has been around for nearly a decade, but only released its first game last year. The team is largely comprised of ex-Telltale, Ubisoft, and Night School Studio talent, which has allowed them to use their narrative expertise for new titles like Dispatch. The 2025 superhero game was a refreshing experience take on a tried and true genre with nuanced relationships, hilarious and compelling writing, and meaningful choices.

Given AdHoc only rose to prominence last year, it's unclear when they were brought on to Until Dawn 2. They could've been a late addition to punch up the game following the success of Dispatch, or Firesprite could've recognized their potential early on and brought them in a couple of years ago. Either way, it's great to see the AdHoc team being utilized on a franchise that means so much to horror fans.

Firesprite also announced that Until Dawn 2 will release on PS5 this January , which is sooner than some would've anticipated. The game was announced earlier this summer and will feature returning characters, such as the mysterious Dr. Hill, from the first game.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: YouTube Star MoistCr1TiKaL Is Making a Full-Length Animated Movie Based on His Godslap Comic, Coming to Theaters in 2028
articles.summary: YouTube star Charlie ‘MoistCr1tikal’ White is the mastermind behind a full-length animated movie adaptation of his very own comic, Godslap, set to release in theaters in 2028.
articles.body:
YouTube star Charles ‘MoistCr1TiKaL’ White is the mastermind behind a full-length animated movie adaptation of his very own comic, Godslap, set to release in theaters in 2028.

The film’s first teaser trailer was published on September 3, 2026, showing off the slick animation and smooth artwork from Powerhouse Animation, best known for its work on Netflix’s Castlevania: Nocturne and Masters of the Universe: Revelation.

As told by White in a YouTube video announcing the news, the Godslap movie follows Aius, a young man with the “incredibly strong gift of slapping.” However, his incredible power has made his father, Darius, extremely overprotective of him, fearing what could happen if he were to venture into the outside world.

First teaser for ‘GODSLAP’, a new animated film based on MoistCr1TiKaL's comic series. The film follows a boy with an extraordinary slapping ability who ventures out into the world for the first time. pic.twitter.com/RfrajR1SuY — DiscussingFilm (@DiscussingFilm) September 3, 2026

First teaser for ‘GODSLAP’, a new animated film based on MoistCr1TiKaL's comic series. The film follows a boy with an extraordinary slapping ability who ventures out into the world for the first time. pic.twitter.com/RfrajR1SuY

“He is now, for the first time, venturing out from his farm where his father Darius has been kind of an overbearing a**hole trying to keep him away from the rest of the world out of fear for what that power could do,” White explained.

The YouTuber revealed that he first approached Powerhouse Animation about the project all the way back in 2018. At the time, however, he was unprepared for the sheer amount of money it’d take to finance such a venture and effectively ghosted the studio, resigning himself to the reality that his dream of adapting Godslap into an animated movie might be too expensive to ever realize.

Years passed… but three years ago, Powerhouse reached out to White saying they were interested in adapting the comic, which is still roughly two years away from being fully finished.

White says that he plans on releasing the movie in theaters, making it the second big influencer-led project to have a theatrical release following Markiplier’s indie horror Iron Lung earlier this year.

White said that he is the “sole financier” of the Godslap movie, and that he and the team behind the comic have been “involved every single step of the way.”

“This has been one of the biggest dreams I’ve had since I was a child, and I believe in it so strongly that I’ve been putting my money where my c**k is — millions, in order to bring this project to life and make it as big, as special, as unique as it can possibly be,” he said.

The YouTuber plans on sharing more information in the coming months, including voice talent, behind-the-scenes info, and more.

Speaking with Deadline , Lyrical Animation's Creative Director, Daniel Dominguez, said the studio, which is co-developing the Godslap movie alongside Powerhouse, have been fans of White for a long time.

“Getting the opportunity to bring his anime-inflected, hilariously violent comic Godslap to life was a dream come true,” he said. “It’s one of the funniest, most non-stop surprising, and thematically urgent comics to come out in the last decade, and a perfect story to adapt as an animated feature.”

White has been involved in quite a few animated projects himself prior to the Godslap movie; gamers will recognize him as the voice of Sonar id Adhoc’s Dispatch , and anime fans might remember that he voiced a character in Netflix’s Baki series.

articles.title: Waffle House Movie in the Works Starring X-Men’s Inde Navarrette
articles.summary: Not content just to appear in Marvel's X-Men reboot, Inde Navarrette has signed on to star in a bizarre sci-fi thriller called The Waffle House Index.
articles.body:
Obsession star Inde Navarrette may have just signed on for Marvel's upcoming X-Men reboot , but that's not stopping her from taking on smaller and weirder projects. Case in point: Navarrette is slated to star in The Waffle House Index, a sci-fi thriller about a Waffle House waitress dealing with an overnight shift from hell.

The news comes courtesy of The Hollywood Reporter . THR writes that the film has just been picked up by Apple Original Films. It features a screenplay by Andrew Nunnelly, one that was featured on the 2025 Black List (a list of the most acclaimed unproduced scripts circulating in Hollywood). The Waffle House Index is slated to be directed by Louis Paxton (The Incomer). The film will be produced by Plan B Entertainment, with Navarrette herself executive producing.

The title of the film refers to the infamous barometer Waffle House restaurants use while under hurricane threat. A Waffle House Index can range from green to yellow to red depending on how severe weather conditions are and whether a given restaurant stays open or not. In short, if the Waffle House Index is red, it's time to panic.

The index may well reach the red zone in this movie, as it's teased that Navarrette's beleaguered character will deal with everything from a rogue gunman to flash floods to crocodile attacks to nuclear missiles and even a hidden bunker located underneath the Waffle House itself (hey, it is a sci-fi movie).

Alongside X-Men, this marks the first new project for Navarrette following her breakout performance in 2026's Obsession. In IGN's Obsession review , Matt Donato writes, "Obsession should and will put Barker on the map as a horror filmmaker you need to watch. Thanks to fantastic turns by Michael Johnston and Inde Navarrette, you'll be addicted to this sour Valentine's Day counterprogramming. The film plays on familiar romance and monkey's paw tropes, turning a wish against the wishee, but Barker's execution takes things to the next level. In the film's simplicity lay the chance to go for broke, putting all efforts into the lengths Nikki is willing to go for her beloved. With that focus and Barker's fearlessness, Obsession becomes one hell of a maximalist ride."

articles.title: Brandon Sanderson Makes the Case for Reading the Project Hail Mary Book Even If You've Seen the Movie Already
articles.body:
Since revealing his new relationship with Hollywood , Brandon Sanderson's weekly podcast has become increasingly focused on movie and book adaptations. This week, he and his co-host Dan Wells dove into the topic of the Project Hail Mary movie, and Sanderson makes a compelling case for reading Andy Weir's book.

"They left out a lot of the science, the try fails, the figuring out how everything works," Sanderson said. He went on to explain that the moment he finds out he's on a spaceship is quite a bit longer in the books compared to the movie, describing the experience as if "you're figuring it out with him, like what is this? What is going on?"

Sanderson still had nothing but positive things to say about the film, saying he thinks "they did a fantastic job." IGN's review of the film reflects his same sentiment, which landed it on our list of the top-reviewed movies of 2026 so far.

As someone who read the book before watching the movie, I definitely agree with Sanderson on this topic. Movies are never going to be able to provide the same level of depth you're going to get from the novel. Andy Weir is great about taking you on a fun journey of details, but a film can't truly show all of that. When you're dealing with a limited runtime, all you can do is enough to make the science feel believable as a plot device. In the books, you get to really dig deep into what the character is experiencing in every scene.

For those who haven't read the book, I highly recommend it. It's also one of my favorite audiobooks . Narrator Ray Porter has an incredibly soothing voice and there are some excellent background sounds that really sell the audio experience. It's an easy transition coming from the movie if you're not used to reading books.

articles.title: Miami-Dade Sheriff and Commissioner Slam City's Proposed GTA 6 Takeover for 'Promoting Fictional Version of Our Community Defined by Crime and Violence'
articles.summary: The Sheriff of Miami-Dade county is speaking out against Miami’s proposal to celebrate the launch of GTA 6 by decking out the city in advertisements for the highly-anticipated game, arguing that it glorifies crime and undermines the efforts of law enforcement.
articles.body:
The Sheriff of Miami-Dade county is speaking out against Miami’s proposal to celebrate the launch of GTA 6 by decking out the city in advertisements for the highly-anticipated game, arguing that it glorifies crime and undermines the efforts of law enforcement.

Grand Theft Auto 6 takes place in Vice City, a fictional version of Miami, Florida. Rockstar took pains to faithfully recreate Miami’s most iconic locales and architecture within the game, with fans already spotting a few real-life locations in the title’s newest trailers.

In late August, local news outlets reported that Miami-Dade County officials had spoken with Rockstar Games about potential plans for a Grand Theft Auto 6-themed takeover of Miami, which included ideas like wrapping the Metro line with Vice City branding, creating Vice City manhole covers, and decking out the Miami International Airport with ‘Welcome to Vice City’ signage.

Even More GTA 6 Screenshots from Rockstar Games

While nothing has been formally approved, it seemed like the city was gung-ho for a partnership with the biggest game of the year… but now, the Miami-Dade county sheriff is bringing those ideas to a screeching halt.

Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz and Commissioner Juan Carlos Bermudez believe that celebrating Grand Theft Auto — a game series famous for allowing players to engage in criminal activity — in such a way would essentially promot a fictionalized, crime-ridden version of their city.

"Grand Theft Auto is a video game franchise built around criminal activity. Its fictional world includes murder, robbery, drug trafficking, carjacking, violence against law enforcement, and other conduct that the men and women of the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office work every single day to prevent," Cordero-Stutz said, per NBC Miami 6.

"At a time when law enforcement is working every day to reduce violent crime, prevent robberies and car thefts, combat drug trafficking, and build stronger relationships between our deputies and the communities we serve, I believe we need to seriously consider the message we send when our own government promotes a fictional identity centered around many of those same crimes."

“I still cannot believe that we are even considering temporarily rebranding important County assets, including Miami International Airport, as 'Vice City Airport,'" Bermudez added. "Miami-Dade County has spent decades building a reputation as a world-class destination for tourism, business, investment, and opportunity. We should be promoting the Miami-Dade we have worked so hard to build, not a fictional version of our community defined by crime and violence."

It’s unclear what the future of Miami’s GTA 6 takeover will look like, now that the county sheriff has spoken out against the idea… but with the title shaping up to be one of the biggest releases in video game history, it certainly seems like a profitable venture, should it actually work out.

The sheriff isn't the only one balking at GTA 6's November 19 launch; spouses across social media have also kicked off a heated debate after claiming that playing the game, which features a relationship mechanic between dual protagonists Jason and Lucia, is tantamount to cheating.

articles.title: Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves Directors Say Film Flopped Due to 'Not-So-Great' Timing
articles.summary: The directors of Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves, John Francis Daley and Jonathan Goldstein, admitted the fantasy flick flopped due to “not-so-great timing” because of The Super Mario Bros. movie and drama with Wizards of the Coast’s proposed D&D licensing changes.
articles.body:
The directors of Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves, John Francis Daley and Jonathan Goldstein, admitted the fantasy flick flopped due to “not-so-great timing” because of The Super Mario Bros. movie and drama with Wizards of the Coast’s proposed D&D licensing changes.

Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves released in March 2023, right around the time that Wizards of the Coast was facing massive backlash from players after confirming planned adjustments to their Open-Gaming License that would have made sweeping changes to rules that allowed creators to make and sell their own content based on the tabletop RPG’s fifth edition.

While they ultimately ended up walking this disastrous decision back , the blowback was enough to negatively impact the movie adaptation, says director John Francis Daley. He claims that this drama, alongside the hugely-successful launch of The Super Mario Bros. Movie around the same time, ultimately overshadowed a film that has since proven to be a hit among fans after the fact.

“It was very much a product of not-so-great timing when the first movie came out,” Daley said in an episode of The Discourse Podcast . “It came out four days before the Super Mario movie, which broke records. It came out a month after Wizards of the Coast changed the official gaming license, prompting many D&D fans to boycott the game, and I don’t think the marketing did enough to tell people who weren’t already fans that this movie might be for them. Yeah, so it was a perfect storm of all of those elements, and we’ll see.”

Honor Among Thieves struggled at the box office, and Paramount has since passed up on making a sequel due to “financial” reasons. But Daley and Goldstein are hopeful that another studio will pick them up to continue telling stories in the Dungeons & Dragons universe.

“Yeah, absolutely,” Goldstein confirmed after being asked if anyone is actively crunching the numbers for a possible sequel. “I think Hasbro is a big believer in it, and if they can figure out a studio partner to make it work, they’ll want to proceed. As are our producers.”

“I mean, look, it’s something that is near and dear to our hearts in that we loved making the first one,” Daley added. “We fell in love with the characters, and there’s so much potential in a sequel because the first act isn’t filled with exposition or introduction to this family that we’ve already become accustomed to. So you can kind of launch right into the story, which is really nice.”

Fans shouldn’t despair; while an Honor Among Thieves sequel is still up in the air, a live-action TV series is officially in the works at Netflix, based on the TTRPG’s gothic-horror world “Ravenloft.” Described as a “prestige fantasy series where adventure collides with gothic horror and tragic romance,” it follows “the making of the vampire Darklord Strahd von Zarovic.”

Even better, a new third-person action-adventure game titled Dungeons & Dragons: Warlock is also in development, set to release sometime in 2027.

articles.title: Blizzard Might Be Teasing A New StarCraft Game
articles.summary: There's something odd happening on the StarCraft website. While the content still features StarCraft Remastered, which launched back in 2017, the page now seems to be glitching out, with various elements, images, and text blocks flickering on-screen randomly. Could Blizzard be teasing a new StarCraft game?
articles.body:
There's something odd happening on the StarCraft website . While the content still features StarCraft Remastered, which launched back in 2017, the page now seems to be glitching out, with various elements, images, and text blocks flickering on-screen randomly. Could Blizzard be teasing a new StarCraft game?

That would make sense. A report earlier this year said that Blizzard had partnered with Korean gaming giant Nexon to develop a new StarCraft shooter. Blizzard declined to comment on the matter at the time, and the partnership remains unconfirmed, but a report yesterday from South Korean newspaper Chosun ( via Wccftech ) reaffirms that Nexon is seeking a license to develop a new StarCraft game.

Meanwhile, Blizzard may have been working on its own new StarCraft game, as per a 2024 job posting for an "upcoming open-world shooter." Reports from that time suggested the title was in development at Blizzard, led by former Far Cry executive producer Dan Hay, who joined the company in 2022.

Another point of evidence is that BlizzCon returns on September 12 after a three-year hiatus , and Blizzard will undoubtedly want to make a splash there with big news beyond its ongoing franchises. There's also a conspicuous hour-long gap on BlizzCon's day-one mainstage programming , while all other panels only have 15 minutes of downtime between them. Sure seems like the place for something that gets announced during the opening ceremonies.

StarCraft as a franchise has sat dormant since 2017's remaster of the original game, which will celebrate its 30th anniversary in 2028. StarCraft 2 launched in 2010, with its subsequent expansions concluding in 2015. Meanwhile, legendary vaporware third-person shooter StarCraft: Ghost was announced in 2002 and eventually confirmed to be cancelled in 2014.

I can't verify exactly how long the glitch effect on the StarCraft website has been live, but I haven't seen anyone talking about it yet, and the most recent Wayback Machine capture of the page from just over a week ago doesn't show the effect (though I can't be sure if the Wayback Machine would properly capture and show it).

It's unclear if this tease is related to Blizzard's own game, the one from the Nexon partnership, if those two games are one in the same, if either of them are StarCraft 3, or none of the above. IGN has reached out to Blizzard for comment on both the tease and the Nexon partnership, and will update this article if we hear back.

Either way, BlizzCon is just over a week away, so a formal announcement could be just on the horizon.

articles.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker's Most Popular Mod Completely Defeats the Purpose of the Game
articles.summary: The Blood of Dawnwalker already has a time-altering mod that largely defeats the purpose of the game.
articles.body:
The Blood of Dawnwalker already has a mod that largely defeats the purpose of the game.

In The Blood of Dawnwalker, a new RPG from ex-CD Projekt Red staff, the player fills the shoes of a man-turned-vampire who has 30 days to save his family. The game has a non-linear story with different approaches, allowing you to progress how you see fit, but there's a catch: Every mission you take on advances the game's 30-day clock . Some quests advance the clock more than others, forcing the player to be thoughtful about quests they accept. Character progression, such as using the skill tree, also advances the clock.

Naturally, some fans don't like the pressure this creates. The clock forces them to make tough decisions; it means you have to be choosey about what you do in the game. With that said, it makes sense that its most popular mod completely removes the tension created by this mechanic. The Better Story Timer mod on NexusMods gives you 90 days to do quests, triple the intended amount. This means you don't really have to be precious about the in-game clock or think too hard about your choices. It removes most, if not all, of the friction in The Blood of Dawnwalker.

Of course, something like this might make sense a couple of months post-release for those who want to play it differently, but it literally just came out today. The mod has been downloaded almost 10,000 times already, meaning it's pretty popular... but some users have expressed annoyance over players not giving the game a chance in the way it was intended.

"Gamers will do anything they can to not experience a game the way the developers intended," said one X/Twitter user . "I think the main issue is that, nowadays, gamers believe every game should be made for them. The issue is that’s rarely the case, and the games that do cater for everyone usually suck. Sometimes, you aren’t the target audience. And that’s perfectly fine."

The Blood of Dawnwalker is intended to be the beginning of a franchise, one that will sprawl across multiple eras, possibly including the modern day based on a previous trailer for the game. It's unclear when future entires will arrive, but currently, The Blood of Dawnwalker is being hailed as a strong RPG in reviews and appears to be off to a strong start commercially.

IGN gave it a 9/10 in its review , praising the inclusion of the in-game clock.

"The Blood of Dawnwalker is my new favorite vampire game and one of the best story-driven RPGs I’ve played in a long time," reads an excerpt from the review. "The day/night cycle that has you juggling human and vampiric forms is awesome, and the constraints placed on how you spend your limited time ends up being one of the coolest, most wonderfully stressful parts of the adventure."

articles.title: Dexter: Resurrection Season 2 Is Bringing Back a Major Dead Character in an Unexpected Way
articles.summary: Dexter: Resurrection Season 2 is bringing back a fan-favorite character that tragically died.
articles.body:
Spoilers for Dexter: Resurrection Season 1 and seemingly Season 2 follow below.

Dexter: Resurrection Season 2 is bringing back a fan-favorite character that tragically died.

Deadline has reported that Angel Batista, played by David Zayas, will return in the next season of Dexter: Resurrection. Batista has been in every single season of Dexter in some form since the very beginning, but he met an unfortunate end in Season 1 of Resurrection. After trying to bring Dexter to justice, he ended up being shot and killed by the season's antagonist, Leon Prater. It was a tragic conclusion to the character's arc and one that punished Dexter for trying to have it all.

However, Batista will be back once again in Season 2. The actor was seen on set filming a scene with Michael C. Hall in Times Square. Interestingly, he was sporting a more colorful outfit than the last time we saw him, with a Hawaiian shirt, his signature hat, and his gun holster. This seems to suggest that Zayas is returning as one of Dexter's ghosts, preserved in an outfit from when he was a detective in Florida. Various characters have appeared after their deaths to guide or antagonize Dexter over the course of the franchise, but they're not literal ghosts. They're more like manifestations of Dexter's conscience, so Batista may represent some kind of internal guilt for the titular serial killer this time around.

His inclusion makes sense, especially as Joey Quinn, another cop from Dexter's past, will also return this season . It's unclear how that story will unravel, but hopefully the writers are smart enough to recognize they can't repeat Batista's arc with another Miami Metro detective. Either way, it seems like we're in for another suspenseful season of Dexter.

Batista also isn't the only dead character returning in Dexter: Resurrection, but the other one may not be as dead as we thought. We won't spoil it here, but you can click here for more details. Dexter: Resurrection Season 2 is expected to premiere sometime this fall.

articles.title: Turkish GTA 6 Fans Want Language Support So Badly, They Professionally Dubbed the Gameplay Reveal
articles.summary: Turkish GTA 6 fans want language support so badly that they went out of their way to professionally dub the game's gameplay reveal.
articles.body:
Turkish GTA 6 fans want language support so badly that they went out of their way to professionally dub its gameplay reveal.

The Turkish gaming community has been asking for more and more studios to add Turkish language support for their games. This has led to massive fan campaigns for titles like 007 First Light , which actually resulted in IO Interactive adding Turkish subtitles to the game. Now, the Turkish gaming community is turning their focus to the most anticipated release of the year, if not the most anticipated game in history: Grand Theft Auto 6.

Fans have been asking Rockstar Games to add Turkish subtitles or voice overs to GTA 6 ahead of its release in November. They aren't just making social media posts tagging Rockstar, either; they actually professionally dubbed and mixed the entire GTA 6 extended look with a whole cast of actors. The Turkish dub went up just a day after the gameplay was released , which means there was a very fast turn around. It's pretty impressive and shows, there are members of the community actively trying to make this a reality.

YouTuber Pintipanda also made a video asking Rockstar to see the potential in localizing GTA 6 for Turkish players. In it, he points out how Turkish-speaking individuals exist in a number of countries outside of Turkey itself, and that GTA 6 is bound to have a wide reach, so it should be as inclusive as possible.

"I know that you guys do these things internally, but if creating a team from zero is hard or you don't have the time or the luxury, you have the money, of course. There is an alternative way to do this. We have world-class Turkish localization teams here. We are playing The Witcher 3 in Turkish, Cyberpunk 2077 in Turkish, Baldur's Gate in Turkish, and Warhammer games in Turkish. As you guessed, these are text-heavy games that we are playing and enjoy in our native country.

"The studios behind these games like CD Projekt Red or Techland, all the studios are getting their investment back with the sales. That's a win-win, that's an alternative way to do these kinds of things. The choice is yours."

Even More GTA 6 Screenshots from Rockstar Games

The creator went on to say he's aware that localizing GTA 6 won't happen overnight, but the community simply wants to be acknowledged by Rockstar as a "starting point." Ultimately, we'll just have to wait and see what happens, but it's clear there is a passionate group of players trying to get the best experience for themselves.

GTA 6 is a little more than two months away now, and Rockstar has its foot on the gas when it comes to marketing. Following the gameplay reveal last week, a bunch of previews of GTA 6 were released from select content creators and IGN itself. This has resulted in no shortage of news and details about the highly-anticipated game. Earlier today, Rockstar and PlayStation also revealed two limited-edition GTA 6-themed PS5 controllers , which will go up for pre-order next week.

articles.title: Elden Ring Director Hidetaka Miyazaki Says He's 'Honestly Not Sure' Where the Rumor About Him Having a Foot Fetish Came From
articles.summary: Dark Souls and Elden Ring director Hidetaka Miyazaki has addressed the rumors that he's got a foot fetish, and he seemed pretty baffled by the whole thing.
articles.body:
Dark Souls and Elden Ring director Hidetaka Miyazaki has addressed the rumors that he's got a foot fetish, and he seemed pretty baffled by the whole thing.

Miyazaki’s games are beloved for their brutal gameplay, grimdark settings, and tortured characters. Of these characters, several of the female bosses, NPCs, and helpers share a common trait: They aren’t wearing any shoes.

The Maiden in Black from Demons’ Souls, Sister Friede, Gwunevere, and Priscilla from the Dark Souls games, and even Malenia in Elden Ring all boast bare feet. (Yes, we know Malenia’s legs were destroyed by the Scarlet Rot, but her brother created prosthetics for her that included highly-detailed feet with individual toes. That still counts!)

Elden Ring - Malenia Blade of Miquella - Action Figure

Over the years, this has sparked an inside joke within the Soulslike community, who lightheartedly figured that Miyazaki must be a foot guy. It was never a serious thing — but he brought it up, totally unprompted, during an interview with The Guardian in September 2026.

Miyazaki was responding to a question about recurring imagery of hands that crops up across most of his games, including his most recent offering, The Duskbloods.

“It’s not necessarily something I’m consistently aware of – maybe it’s something subconscious coming through,” he answered. “Take a look online and there’s a rumor that I have a bit of a thing for feet, but I’m not honestly sure where this comes from. I feel like I’m trying to depict some side of human nature or the human existence that is difficult to describe.”

Hey, we’re not gonna yuck anyone’s yum, but it sounds like this wasn’t even a thought in Miyazaki’s mind when he made these character designs. Instead, he was trying to depict some kind of overarching symbolism about humanity within those characters’ appearances, which includes themes like “ruin and rebirth.”

“[Ruin and rebirth] is an ongoing theme in a lot of my games, I realise,” he added in his interview with The Guardian. “That theme on a cosmological scale applies to The Duskbloods as an interesting philosophical area to explore.

“If we have two ideas of a brighter or dark future, I would tend to sway towards the darker one,” Miyazaki says. “[But] if you explore the ruin and the decay in those worlds, it also lets you explore some chance of rebirth, and I think having that tiny pinprick of light or hope can be something beautiful, something fleeting,” he continued.

Speaking of The Duskbloods, IGN’s Michael Higham described the upcoming title as “FromSoftware’s most complex and interesting game yet” in his hands-on preview. In the lead-up to its launch, he also got the chance to chat with Miyazaki about the game, who told us a bit more about its development process and assured us that yes, Fromsoft is still interested in making single-player games.

articles.title: 4K Blu-ray Players Are Selling Out at Major Retailers as Prices Quickly Increase
articles.body:
I've been thinking about buying a good 4K Blu-ray player for a while now. Here at IGN we regularly cover new 4K movie releases, and I myself have started my own modest collection. As I was browsing Labor Day sales this week looking for a discount, I was unpleasantly surprised by what I found.

I knew a dedicated 4K player was going to be an expensive purchase, but it seems it's gotten even more expensive this year specifically. Prices have skyrocketed on some brands, while some of the best Blu-ray players IGN has been recommending for years are just completely out of stock. It's apparently not the best time to be buying a 4K Blu-ray player.

So what exactly is going on here? Why is there suddenly such a high demand for these seemingly niche devices? Well, the most plausible answer can be found in the market for physical media. There was a bit of a aresurgence in the 4K Blu-ray market last year, with the 4K category actually seeing growth for the first time in years. Fast forward to this year, and actually owning your media is becoming quite popular again across multiple generations. Even Pokémon is cashing in on the upward trend in 2026.

More people buying 4K and Blu-ray discs doesn't necessarily translate to more Blu-ray players being manufactured. On top of that, the fact that Sony has made the decision to go entirely digital by 2028 has only exacerbated the problem. For many folks, a PlayStation 5 or an Xbox Series X was an easy way to access their 4K collection. With console prices rising and the need to purchase a disc drive separately, a dedicated 4K Blu-ray player is still the most affordable option right now.

Should You Wait to Buy a 4K Blu-ray Player?

Like any economic market, high-demand and low supply is going to mean higher prices. Panasonic and Sony are two of the only companies still making 4K players for average consumers, and unlike TVs, they rarely release new models. Popular 4K players like the Panasonic DP-UB9000 and the Sony UBP-X700M have been around for years and were the first to start going out of stock this year.

All-in-all, it's not a very good time to buy a 4K Blu-ray player at a good price. Considering the upward trend of 4K movies, I'd expect Blu-ray players to eventually become more of a commodity item in the next few years as new companies flood the market. Until then, don't expect prices to drop at all.

With that being said, right now is a good time to buy 4K Blu-ray discs . Major retailers are regularly discounting movies and box sets throughout the year and you can usually find a great price if you're patient. If you already have a way to play 4K discs , it's a great time to be a collector.

articles.title: Furious Is the Best New Show You’re Not Watching Yet
articles.summary: Hulu's eight-episode crime thriller’s first season starring Emmy Rossum and Lola Petticrew just wrapped up this week and its incredible finale locked in this show as my favorite new drama — and maybe TV show, period — of the year.
articles.body:
If you’re in need of a new show to binge over this (or any) long weekend, I’m imploring you: Watch Furious. The eight-episode crime thriller’s first season just wrapped up this week and its incredible finale locked in this show as my favorite new drama — and maybe TV show, period — of the year.

It’s already been a good year for TV show debuts. A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms had a built-in audience, being part of the Game of Thrones-verse, but stood out with its charming buddy duo in Dunk and Egg. Widow’s Bay grew into the breakout TV hit of early summer, with people fawning over its idiosyncratic genre blend and stellar ensemble. Lanterns is doing pretty well, too (when it’s not pissing some people off ). But Hulu’s Furious is the latest surprise show that has broken containment, growing week-over-week — the finale had 90% more views than the premiere, which already cracked the bottom of Nielson’s streaming charts, according to Variety . It’s already been greenlit for a second season . Basically, Furious is special and people are noticing.

Created by Elizabeth Meriweather, who’s best known for New Girl, Furious is just barely based on the 1987 movie Black Widows, which starred Debra Winger and Theresa Russell, but toss aside any assumptions you might make based on that creative pedigree combo. It’s hardly a breezy half-hour sitcom, though it knows how to deploy humor to cut through the bleakness, and has almost nothing in common with the ‘80s film aside from the women serial killer/Fed dynamic.

Furious is often a difficult watch based on the details of its dead-serious subject matter, but it has an almost unbelievable iron grip over its pacing and tone. Things will happen that make your stomach churn, but it never crosses over into exploitation, handling all of the show’s many thorny complexities head-on with care. The mounting tension is so dialed in that scenes — sometimes action-driven, other times just an interrogation — feel palpably dangerous, creating that propulsive “I gotta watch another episode” itch. Frankly, I’m envious of those starting it now, when you don’t have to wait a week between episodes. (At the same time, I’m also relieved it got the old-school weekly episode release treatment to find an audience and wasn’t dumped all at once.)

On paper, Furious may sound like any other decent cat-and-mouse crime drama, but it really is so much more. That’s in no small part thanks to the depth of characters and electric performances, especially from its core cast of women characters, all (as the title implies) of whom are full of justified rage. Petticrew — who was also great in Say Nothing, last year’s excellent Hulu series about the Irish Republican Army during The Troubles — gives Catherine a trauma-laden, erratic unpredictability with huge emotional peaks and valleys, and yet never becomes hammy. Rossum — probably best known for Shameless and Phantom of the Opera — simmers as Alice, who can be stoic, cruel, selfish, and compassionate all at once. Perhaps best of all is Quincy Tyler Bernstine — while lauded for stage acting, she’s made plenty of prestige-y TV appearances — as Nora Washington, Alice’s boss and Greek mythology enthusiast who doesn’t waste a single word during her screen time. The men are pretty good, too: Scoot McNairy as the exhausted good cop, Jake Lacy as the insatiable bad cop, Rob Yang as a sort-of-stupid FBI agent, Danny McCarthy as a corrupt jerk FBI ASAC, and Steve Way as the hopelessly romantic and mold-breaking comic relief .

I’m being purposefully cagey about the grimier plot specifics because I really think new watchers are best served in knowing as little as possible before going in, learning the dark, reality-coded secrets of Furious as you watch. But if you want to take a dive into a messed-up series that will almost definitely be in Emmy conversations next year, you know where to look.

Leanne Butkovic (she/they) is an Editorial Programming Manager at IGN, where they've also written about TV, movies, and games.

articles.title: Metal Gear Solid Master Collection Vol. 2 Review, Gameplay Impressions, Videos and Top Features
articles.summary: Metal Gear Solid Master Collection Vol. 2 from developer Konami brings modern beloved entries of the historic series to the forefront of gaming once more.
articles.body:
Metal Gear Solid Master Collection Vol. 2 from developer Konami brings modern beloved entries of the historic series to the forefront of gaming once more.

The Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection from 2023 got the ball rolling with a generation of stealth classics with the perplexing, memorable overall narrative found early in the series.

Fast forward to now, Master Collection Vol. 2 brings 2008's Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots and 2010's Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker to the limelight, finally freeing the former from its PlayStation 3 prison and latter from the handheld PSP once again.

Chicken equity? This may be the wildest jersey number trade yet

Guns of the Patriots finally being accessible on modern hardware would be merit enough to demand returning and new players alike grab Vol. 2. Tacking on the extra goodies and modern trappings just makes it all the better.

At the time of release, MGS4 was nearly unmatched in terms of visuals and overall immersion during moment-to-moment gameplay. The jarring sound design and stellar graphics did heavy lifting. Obviously, those things have aged since the PS3 era, to say the least.

Even so, 4K does MGS4 some serious justice. Everyone knew it looked good back then, but seeing it souped up in 2026 and holding its own despite being a PS3 title is…pretty impressive.

As most could have probably predicted, the gameplay holds up even better than the presentation.

At the time, Guns of the Patriots was a major shift for Metal Gear Solid. It left the comfortable confines of the past and decided to start being a standard-bearer instead, putting players in control of an AAA action experience.

In current times, the over-the-shoulder camera still feels modern, as does the ability to change things to first-person.

The stealth itself and active camo system is still one of the best in gaming, ever. It holds up rather surprisingly well, in part because the stealth genre, Splinter Cell included, sort of imploded over the last decade or so.

But much of it is simply because it was so good , even back then. The sheer number of ways to approach a situation, funny enemy AI and punchiness of it all meshed perfectly with the ambiance and story.

Then there's Peace Walker, the game that first really leaned into the base-building aspects of later entries. Its shocking number of missions and the quick-hitting format of those went on to influence plenty, including much of what people see in mobile games these days.

That's a compliment, by the way. Few mobile games come close. Peace Walker is a blast in near-2027, even if the almost-intimidating number of missions starts to get a little repetitive.

There isn't much all that different with these classics here. Stellar gameplay, both for powerful consoles or handhelds of the era, still holds up well and is a blast, hence the classical nature of both in the first place.

This is Metal Gear Solid. Don't expect to enter Guns of the Patriots understanding much of anything. That even goes for those who have played it in the past.

Kidding aside, it's still gripping and memorable. And if we're talking about story beats like say, algorithms influencing things and privatization, etc., it sure feels right at home in modern times.

The five acts in Guns of the Patriots remain refreshingly diverse in locale and execution, be it slinking through a battleship or sneaking around various bits of nature.

It's a narrative feast of unique goofiness to this day, with the boogeyman "nanomachines" explaining away anything that might not make a lick of sense. Snake wants to off Liquid Ocelot, is the tried-and-true basic premise, with lots of unforgettable, weird boss battles and stuff standing in his way.

Peace Walker's tale, on the other hand, is decidedly more, well, handheld. There are some comicbook-like trappings and memorable stuff going on, but the difference is obvious. Again, not a bad thing. For some, it'll harken back to some nostalgia bits of handheld glory days.

Master Collection Vol. 2 runs well, as expected, but it makes some head-scratching decisions, too. There are multiple launchers for the game on PC, which is a little odd. There's a separate launcher for bonus features, for example.

Even so, the sheer amount of content here is a bit staggering. There's a little Game Boy title tucked into here as well, plus the yawning expanse of what is essentially a Metal Gear Wikipedia included for good measure.

Guns of the Patriots is the real treat here for technical reasons and for the sheer fact it's an all-time classic that happens to, sort of wrap up the overall story and end the Hideo Kojima era.

That's not meant to sell Peace Walker short because it deserves its flowers for evolving not just the mobile game space, but future entries like MGS5 heavily took from it, too.

Taken as a whole, though, Guns of the Patriots is the far bigger deal here. And taking into account the extra stuff, sheer runtime and overall importance, one could argue this is far, far more important than the first Master Collection release.

No complaints, though, regardless. As the most important entry in this resurgence of Metal Gear Solid, this has been a long, long time coming and it's one of the few packages to truly be worth the wait.
